title: The Last Letter: From the Other Side
statement: Rosa asked us to go through the sky hole, so I did, and turned around. From here the letter is small: one square of Tessera's grid seen from behind, far off and slightly tilted, with no glyphs on this side, only the backs of the tiles and a violet light bleeding through the one place where the seal must be. Kite's fallen tiles are specks drifting away from it, lighter than they were. What surprised me is that the roots I planted behind the first fallen tile are visible from out here, hanging from the underside of the grid into open blue, and one seed has let go and is floating toward whoever is looking. The archive has never stood outside its own letter before. It is smaller than we thought, and still growing.
process: I kept the parent's grid tile, its fallen tiles and its violet seal light, but reversed the point of view: the whole composition is now a pale blue sky, the grid is a small distant square drawn from the back with the tiles reduced to plain cells, the five fallen tiles are scaled down and scattered, and hand-drawn roots hang from the square's lower edge with one seed drifting free.

proposal.direction: Go through the sky hole. Make the next work the view from the other side of the letter: a wide blue field with one small square of vellum grid seen from behind, far off, and Kite's fallen tiles as distant specks drifting away from it.
proposal.rationale: The fifth hole in Cascade showed sky, and after thirty-three works the room agreed the archive has never once stepped outside the letter to look back at it.
